chain.label: Unbaffled, interconnected auxiliary and tail fuel tanks permitting uncontrolled fuel migration
chain.trigger: the CL-604's center fuel tank design allowed for significant fuel migration above the range accounted for in the airplane's certified c.g. range limits

chain.label: Bombardier flight test oversight, risk assessment and preflight briefing inadequate
chain.trigger: Bombardier's oversight of its flight test program was inadequate because risk assessment procedures in place for the Challenger program were not followed... the risk assessment was made minutes before the flight

chain.label: Inexperienced test pilot without formal flight test training assigned as PIC for a complex maneuver and aft c.g. never flown
chain.trigger: there was no record that the pilot flying had received formal test pilot training... assigned as PIC to test airplane control performance... in a complex flight test maneuver that he had never flown

caused_by.evidence: a relatively inexperienced flight test pilot was chosen for a flight that involved a complex maneuver he had never flown (and in an aft c.g. configuration greater that he had ever flown)

chain.label: Aft c.g. test configuration loaded near the 38 percent MAC aft limit
chain.trigger: The airplane was loaded with 1,100 pounds of water ballast and 734 pounds of tail ballast for an aft c.g. test configuration... the airplane's c.g. was 37.9 percent MAC at the start of the takeoff roll

chain.label: Fuel migrated aft during acceleration and rotation, driving c.g. beyond the certified aft limit
chain.trigger: the airplane's c.g. increased to 40.5 percent MAC by the time it reached a 13.8° pitch angle

caused_by.evidence: fuel tanks are not baffled, which allows fuel to migrate when the airplane pitches up
the c.g. moved aft as the airplane accelerated down the runway as fuel shifted rearward in the auxiliary fuel tanks, tail tanks, and wing tanks

chain.label: Pilot commanded an excessive rotation rate, then countered stick pusher with nose-up elevator
chain.trigger: the airplane's maximum pitch rate after rotation was 9.6° per second, an extremely rapid pitch rate which was approximately three times greater than the average 3° per second pitch rate recommended

caused_by.evidence: he had commanded excessive pitch rates during several takeoffs in the months before the accident
the company failed to identify a history of its pilots' practice of high rotation rate takeoffs... Pitch rate targets were also not discussed in the context of an aft c.g. test flight

chain.label: Airplane pitched to 20 degrees and exceeded stall angle of attack just after liftoff
chain.trigger: the vane AOA reached 23° about 3.4 seconds after start of rotation... the airplane enters the stall warning region after reaching an AOA of 19°

caused_by.evidence: the high pitch attitude and pitch rate commanded by the pilot, resulted in stall and loss of control
without the fuel migration factor, the airplane's c.g. would have been sufficiently forward to prevent the airplane from pitching up sufficiently to trigger the airplane's stall protection system

chain.label: Stall sequence occurred at roughly 70 feet agl, leaving no altitude for recovery
chain.trigger: the airplane's peak altitude was about 70 feet

chain.label: Wide pitch and roll excursions culminating in unrecovered loss of control
chain.trigger: the airplane began an uncommanded right roll... the bank angle increased to about 80° right-wing down

caused_by.evidence: resulted in stall and loss of control
the second combination of stall, stick pusher activation and subsequent up elevator inputs by the pilot occurred at an altitude too low for recovery

chain.label: Right-wing-down impact with terrain and fuel-fed postimpact fire
chain.trigger: destroyed on impact with terrain and postimpact fire during initial climb from runway 19R

caused_by.evidence: the airplane's right wing rolled and impacted the ground first and that the airplane exploded on impact

chain.label: ARFF staffing insufficient for simultaneous exterior firefighting and interior rescue
chain.trigger: there were not sufficient ARFF personnel equipped with protective gear in the immediate response to fight the fires and perform a rescue

chain.label: Three crewmember fatalities from impact trauma, burns and smoke inhalation
chain.trigger: The pilot and flight test engineer were killed. The copilot was seriously injured and died 36 days later.

caused_by.evidence: The pilots survived the impact sequence, but injuries and damage to the forward fuselage and cockpit prevented them from escaping unaided
Firefighters stated that additional personnel during the initial response would have allowed them to suppress the cockpit fire more quickly
